# PR #2737: Patch: the fuzz monitor checks that no unit token reaches a pile and that a position switch spends the exertion an attack needs

Closes #2690

## Summary

Adds fuzz invariants I11 and I12:

- I11 rejects definition-level Unit tokens in graveyards, exile, or held cards while allowing Spell tokens.
- I12 independently shadows position-switch and attack exertion, including Deft, Windfury, forced attacks, re-entry, kill refreshes, and R1202 substitutes.
- Duos runs the same checks per duel.
- Fuzz and fused-pair documentation now describes I1–I12.

No new ruling was needed because §3, §4.1, R11, R49, R636, and R1202 settle the behavior.

## Review findings

Both I12 findings held.

- A later declaration incorrectly erased a spent switch even when the attacker’s `afterAttack` hook refreshed nothing. I12 now requires the resulting field state to independently show the switch exertion was reset.
- R1202 reconciliation used the physical substitute’s `attacker_id`. It now resolves `instead_of` first and attributes exertion and kill credit to the original declarer.

Added regressions for both cases; each failed before the fix and passes afterward.

The validation finding also held. This pass completed the permitted scoped validation. Tools all-target clippy remains blocked before compilation because the offline runner cannot download `ryu 1.0.23`; tools binary clippy passes. Full suites were not run because the pass instructions reserve them for CI. The supplied review reports all three 200-seed fuzz waves passed.

Passed:

- All 25 `rules::invariants` tests
- Both new focused I12 regressions
- 10 R1869002 kill-refresh tests
- Engine all-target clippy with `testkit`
- Tools binary clippy
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `git diff --check`
- Catalog, patches, and spec checks

The final branch changes only the five planned engine/tools files, with no generated, gameplay-reducer, ruling, or forbidden-path changes.

### Not approved

After all 3 rounds the reviewer still had blocking findings, so this is a draft and will not merge by itself.

# #2690: Patch: the fuzz monitor checks that no unit token reaches a pile and that a position switch spends the exertion an attack needs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The random-game tester plays thousands of games through the engine and checks a list of rules after every move. Two rules the spec states plainly are not on that list: a unit token stops existing when it leaves the field, so it never lands in a graveyard or exile pile; and a unit gets one action a turn, an attack or a change of position, unless it has Deft. If the engine ever broke either, the tester would not notice. Once built, it checks both, so a bug that sends a token to the graveyard, or lets a unit switch and then attack, fails CI with its seed.

## Why
- §3 (`spec/03-zones.md:9`): Graveyard, “Unit tokens never enter it; spell tokens do.” §3.2 (`:34`): unit tokens cease to exist when they leave the field for any reason (R11).
- §4.1 (`spec/04-combat.md:8-9`): “Each unit has one exertion per turn: one attack or one position switch. A unit with Deft may do both (R49).”, and a Windfury unit's first attack spends the exertion a switch needs (R636).
- The monitor is `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`, I1–I10 (header `:46-150`). None scans a pile for unit tokens: `is_unit_token_def` (`:536`) is read only by I6's lineage. I2 counts only `attackDeclared` (`:2332` on) and I4(b) only `exertion.attacked`; nothing reads `exertion.switched`, `positionSwitched` or Deft. I8 cannot see a switch rule broken, since the listing and the reducer share one check (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:178-191`, `:275-305`).
- R11 is kept by many separate paths, among them `zones.rs:594-597` (`is_unit_token`, which reads the type the card shows now, so a token set face-down reads as what it was set as), `effects/hold.rs:122`, `effects/transform.rs:130-135`, `effects/destroy.rs:129` and the sandbox's own graveyard push (`sandbox.rs:263-270`). Exertion is reset in several places too (`turn.rs:274-306`, `combat.rs:219-234`, the kill credit's fresh exertion in `effects/statuses.rs:81-106`).

## Proposal
- I11, after every action: no card whose definition is a unit token (`is_unit_token_def`, by definition, not by face) sits in either side's graveyard or exile, or in `state.held`.
- I12, beside I2's shadow: record a chosen `switchPosition` that emits `positionSwitched` per unit, keyed by turn and stint (`stint_of`); flag a switch or a declared attack in the same stint and turn that the unit's exertion did not allow, Deft read through the layers (`keywords_now`), Windfury's first attack spending the switch (R636), a kill credit's fresh exertion and a re-entry resetting it as I2 already treats them.
- Run both in the Duos per-duel monitor too, and plant a failing state for each in the monitor's tests, as #2568 did for I10.
- Run `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `--handicap` and `--duos`; a real violation found is fixed in the engine with its seed pinned, or split into its own issue if large.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (header list and checks), `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` (its doc lines that list the checks)
- SPEC §3, §3.2, §4.1; R11, R49, R636

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A planted state with a unit token in a graveyard, in exile and in `held` each fails I11; a spell token in a graveyard passes.
- [ ] A planted non-Deft unit that switched and then declares an attack in the same stint fails I12; the same with Deft passes; a Windfury unit that attacked once and then switches fails.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `--handicap` and `--duos` pass, or each failure is fixed or filed with its seed.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, clippy and fmt pass.

## Size and risks
Medium: about 70 lines in the monitor and two planted tests. Risk: a first run may find false positives, as I6's did; each is fixed in the oracle with a comment naming the seed, and a real engine bug found is the point.
